title: Eliminating Tokamak Disruptions with Feedback
abstract: Tokamak disruptions caused by tearing modes can be prevented with magnetic feedback. A database of DIII-D locked mode disruptions provides criteria for major disruptions. The main criterion is that the   q = 2 rational surface must be sufficiently close to the resistive wall surrounding the plasma to interact with it. This is shown in simulations of a sequence of model equilibria derived from the database. If the wall is ideally conducting, major disruptions do not occur. Magnetic feedback emulates a conducting wall, and can prevent major disruptions. Feedback coils must be designed appropriately, otherwise they are not effective in disruption prevention. Simulations of a model of MST also show the q = 2 criterion for major disruptions, as well as feedback stabilization. Feedback offers an attractive alternative to disruption mitigation by impurity injection.
